chunks: Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from ʿImrān ibn Mūsā, from Hārūn ibn Muslim, from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said:

Taqiyyah was mentioned one day in the presence of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام), so he said: “By Allah, if Abū Dharr knew what was in the heart of Salmān, he would have killed him, while the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) had indeed established brotherhood between them.”

So what do you think of the rest of creation? Indeed, the knowledge of the scholars is difficult, exceedingly difficult; none can bear it except a sent Prophet, or a brought-near angel, or a believing servant whose heart Allah has tested for faith.”
Then he said: “Salmān only became one of the scholars because he is a man from us, Ahl al-Bayt; therefore, for that reason, I have attributed him to the scholars.”

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: the Household of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: prudential concealment or guardedness in matters of faith
key_terms.الْإِيمَانِ: faith firmly established in the heart
key_terms.صَعْبٌ مُسْتَصْعَبٌ: extremely difficult and hard to bear
key_terms.عِلْمَ الْعُلَمَاءِ: the profound knowledge possessed by the true scholars
key_terms.مَلَكٌ مُقَرَّبٌ: an angel brought near to Allah
key_terms.نَبِيٌّ مُرْسَلٌ: a Prophet sent by Allah with revelation

ai.seo_question: Why does this hadith say that the knowledge of the scholars is difficult and that Salmān was counted among Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the realities of the knowledge associated with the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام) are profoundly difficult and cannot be borne except by those specially prepared by Allah. It also highlights the rank of Salmān by linking him to Ahl al-Bayt and classifying him among the scholars. The report is significant in showing the depth, gravity, and restricted capacity required to receive higher religious knowledge.
